# [CS079] HTTP Routing in Data Layer (go.architecture.http-in-data-layer)

A package named repository, dao, model, store or storage registers HTTP handlers with http.HandleFunc.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | LOW |
| **Category** | Architecture |
| **CWE** | - |
| **OWASP** | - |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Routes registered from the data layer couple storage to the transport, register handlers as a side effect of importing a storage package, and bypass the middleware the transport layer applies. Register routes where the server is assembled and let the data layer expose functions.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
// package repository
func init() {
	http.HandleFunc("/orders", listOrders)
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
// package api
func Routes(mux *http.ServeMux, h *Handler) {
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /orders", h.ListOrders)
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [go.architecture.http-in-data-layer]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    go.architecture.http-in-data-layer: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore go.architecture.http-in-data-layer -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** go.architecture.http-in-data-layer
```
